notes.title: August Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
[p]Hello raiders!

We are back with our weekly update, this time focusing on the new Hell Galaxy patch.
[/p][p]Since the release of the first patch two weeks ago, we have been busy working on improvements, taking your feedback into account. As we mentioned before, with this patch our goal was to add more depth and awareness to the choices each raider makes when building their main weapon of survival, the mechanical Body made of cold metal. To achieve this we introduced a series of adjustments in that direction.
[/p][p]The overall Value of the ship has been made much more central and visible, so you can clearly see how it changes when you swap modules and how it affects the main characteristics of your ship, such as speed and damage.
To communicate these changes more clearly we also reworked parts of the UI. We introduced a new speed indicator, and the most noticeable change is in the ship summary menu. Several details have been clarified to help you manage the Value of your ship, giving you an immediate sense of how powerful your Body really is. This makes changing modules even more critical to your survival during exile in Neterun.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/288089f153c98e997afdd05233f149d6d82cc36a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We also fixed some major bugs, including issues with loot interactions and one that prevented repairs on certain parts of the Kaledos station in the Outpost located in the Core region.
At the moment, after the update, loading an old save may cause problems with ship composition when upgrading. We are working to resolve this issue as soon as possible. For more details, you can check the dev log released alongside the patch:
[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2513490/view/521974358344728742"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]We are already working on the next patch, which will focus on combat and bring a new set of feedback-driven improvements aimed at making battles even more immersive.
[/p][p]That is all for this week. As we dive back into our dangerous galaxy, we look forward to seeing you again in the next dev diary.
[/p][p]Farewell, raiders![/p]

notes.title: August Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
[p]Hello raiders!
[/p][p align="justify"]Welcome to our second August dev diary. Today we return to our series on module creation, this time focusing on a piece from the fearsome Iron Guild, one of the toughest raider groups Neterun has ever seen.
In our last updates, we talked about the different styles of the Iron Guild and the Gold Guild. The Iron Guild leans into brute force with functional, kinetic weapons. The Gold Guild, on the other hand, is more like a cult devoted to gold, using it to craft elegant, almost ceremonial arms.
But things in Neterun are never that simple. Sure, Iron Raiders love rocket launchers and gatling guns, but they are not against using energy weapons. This brings us to today’s focus, the Collimator Fe-1.
[/p][p align="justify"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/bb92439b612805d56fc2a12fdf2b201254d5650a.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="justify"]The one in the image above was one of our first versions of this agile Iron laser. We aimed for an aggressive look from the start, with a sharp, triangular silhouette. The teeth around the muzzle make it look like a mouth ready to bite, exactly the kind of style the Iron Raiders go for.
[/p][p align="justify"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/f872627389aeff884aed0af8fa18555c331f9ad8.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="justify"]From there, we added the classic energy vents you would expect on a laser module, giving it a charged and powerful feel. At its core, the weapon uses technology inspired by the massive cages found in certain corners of the galaxy. In the game’s lore, it is still produced by Cagetastic, the company that created the cages.
[/p][p align="justify"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/98793d55420dac15c4a166f379141aea6a661fc0.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="justify"]We finished it off with signature Iron Guild touches. The chains, for example, are a recurring element we have used on other Iron gear, helping it feel right at home in the guild’s arsenal. Many shields of the Gold Raiders, the Iron Guild’s eternal rivals, have already fallen to the Collimator Fe-1.
[/p][p align="justify"]That is all for this entry. Thanks for reading and see you in the next one.
[/p][p align="justify"]Farewell, raiders![/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary New Patch
notes.notes:
[p]Hello raiders![/p][p]
Welcome to the first official dev diary of August. Last week, our usual weekly post was replaced by the announcement of the Early Access launch, which finally happened after many sleepless nights in the Galaxy of Neterun.[/p][p]
So, how are things going after launch? We're currently working on several fronts, including some of the issues you've reported. Your feedback has been incredibly valuable and we really appreciate it. 

Yesterday we released the first patch, which addresses one of the most frequently reported issues: the settings menu, especially audio and video options. We wanted to respond quickly to this critical feedback from you raiders and we hope this update makes the game more enjoyable and complete.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/f89c85c6fc941b959406a6c04a76312eba4b9101.png"][/img][/p][p]For the next patch, we are working on a series of balance adjustments to make module changes more impactful in combat and to increase the strategic value of your Body composition. The patch will also include an update to the enemy skill system to add more depth to combat. 
[b]
[/b]We are also working on optimization, which will be improved regularly. We know that some of you have experienced performance issues and we are actively working to address them.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/b5f5432361ab33d47ad5ac39b19f4eee6045b755.png"][/img]
This is how we're preparing for the weeks ahead. We're genuinely happy not just because Hell Galaxy is finally out, but also because of the feedback you're sharing, which helps us understand where to go next and what needs improvement. All of this is thanks to you.
[/p][p]Stay in touch with us. If you haven’t already, join our Discord server to share your thoughts or simply be part of the raiders community.
[/p][p]We hope you found this update interesting and look forward to seeing you in the next entry.

notes.title: Hell Galaxy Out Now!
notes.notes:
[p]Hello raiders!
[/p][p]Today is a very special day: Hell Galaxy is finally available in Early Access on Steam! 
[/p][p]It’s been an intense period of work, and we’ve put a lot of care and effort into creating something fun to play. Your exile in the Galaxy of Neterun will be full of surprises, and we’re really excited to see you dive into the dangerous world we’ve built.  
[/p][p]In this version, you’ll explore the first two raider-colonized areas of Neterun: Limbo and The Core. These zones are packed with quests, enemies, strange alien monuments, hostile raiders ready to tear you apart, and bizarre galactic creatures that will attack both your metal body and your mind, the only biological part that remains after a raider is extracted and installed into a ship. 
[/p][p]This is just the beginning. We’re actively developing Hell Galaxy, adding new content and improving what’s already there. Being able to do this together with you, our community, means a lot to us. We’re eager to hear your feedback so we can continue building this new universe with you and for you. 
[/p][p]We hope you enjoy the game, that you can feel the work behind it, and that your feedback helps us improve and expand the experience to make your time in the galaxy as fun and engaging as possible. 
[/p][p]This is the beginning of your journey through the coils of Neterun.

notes.title: July Dev Diary #4
notes.notes:
[p]Hello raiders![/p][p]Welcome back to our weekly update. We're continuing our series on the development of some of the modules you'll encounter in Hell Galaxy. In previous entries, we looked at Imperial and Iron Guild weapons. Today we're switching things up again with a look at the creation of a Gold laser weapon.[/p][p]The Gold Guild, eternal rivals of the Iron Guild, were another major raider faction during the early stages of Neterun’s colonization. Unlike the Iron Raiders, they favor more scientifically advanced weaponry and have a much more refined aesthetic. They’re devoted to what they consider a raider deity: the god of gold reveals himself through the guild leader.
Here's one of the guild’s most powerful lasers: the Kubeam, shown here in its early concept form.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/282b04cdbc30fad1da63c75752af2a89300a924c.jpg"][/img]
As you can tell, the Gold Guild’s style is very different from what we've shown in previous posts. Technology, elegance, and power define the Gold aesthetic. It’s aggressive, but with a polished look. The divinity they worship must shine through in every detail. We used a lot of circular elements, the "perfect" shape, to suggest the divine connection these raiders believe they experience in battle.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/844adf669c9d1cc3b03048be6ad64aced8cacae1.jpg"][/img][/p][p]In this blockout phase, we focused on some of the standout details from the concept. The long tips, for example, are designed to concentrate the beam on targets for maximum damage. Take note of the Kubeam’s power cores, with their semi-transparent central sections, and the flowing, regal outer decorations. A kind of majesty that borders on the sacred.[/p][p]The weapon is finished with the signature style of the Gold Guild. Intricate engravings on the plates enhance the overall design, adding a final touch of destructive elegance to the Kubeam.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/d15bec4140cea9278d3303bb8a5934c2b85d5ade.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Here’s the final, complete image of the weapon. We’ll see you in the next dev diary![/p][p]Farewell, raiders![/p]

notes.title: July Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
[p]Hello raiders![/p][p]Here we are, finally, with a new dev diary. Today we’re talking about the creation of another module. But this time, enough with the Imperial style. We’re diving into an Iron Guild module, specifically a gatling gun called the Wastemaker.[/p][p]The Iron Guild is one of the factions formed by the raiders of Neterun during colonization. Iron raiders are tough, battle-hardened warriors who are always looking for a fight. Their neural activity spikes during combat, and their metal bodies are equipped with solid, dependable modules built to deliver firepower and intimidate. The Wastemaker is a perfect fusion of these traits.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/21f1634ec8b51e3ed13ee9b791ff5afc67ac2322.png"][/img]
The Wastemaker needs no lengthy introduction. So many of the Iron Guild’s enemies have fallen to its scorching barrels that it has become one of the most respected weapons among Guild members. We wanted to steer clear of the cobbled-together look typical of some Imperial modules. Instead, we went through several design iterations to give it a worn, battle-tested feel, scratched and weathered but without adding too much visual noise.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/fdd5ec99b615267fde11515e8293aecf34cfec87.png"][/img]
The Wastemaker features a cooling system that prevents it from overheating too quickly. This allows it to keep firing and gives enemies little chance to escape. It's a reliable, lightweight weapon that punches through opponents with a steady stream of rounds, significantly boosting a raider’s chances of victory.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/c6e9f361fabfff35abc1f9fe1dc31018648ffcce.png"][/img][/p][p]That wraps up this dev diary. We hope you enjoyed the read, and we’ll catch you in the next one.[/p][p]Farewell, raiders![/p]

notes.title: July Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
[p]Hello raiders![/p][p]Welcome to the second July entry. We love giving you a peek into our creative process, so we’re continuing our series focused on module development. This time, we’re introducing an imperial laser-class weapon. [/p][p]Meet the K&B Beamplier, a powerful energy weapon perfect for raiders looking to break through enemy shields quickly. The Beamplier was designed alongside the gatling gun we featured in the last entry. It shares the same aggressive style and captures that apocalyptic galaxy weapon vibe. We went through more iterations for this one, though.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/614acff746ea7902fd70636a17e0cbe33ab5e101.png"][/img]
Once we settled on the Beamplier’s distinct V-shaped muzzle, we chose the more aggressive variant, in line with the style of imperial weapons and the aesthetic of K&B, one of the major manufacturers in the Hell Galaxy universe.
The laser’s structure is packed with detail. A thin metal mesh is all that protects the Beamplier’s battery, which delivers just the right amount of energy to this compact, easy-to-mount weapon. Power cables connect the energy core to the neural transmitter, a key component found in every module, allowing raiders to control them using only mental pulses.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/c74a680102e59cfa2331a401377067552f7bea38.png"][/img]
The detailed 3D modeling emphasizes the energy section and its raw power. The Beamplier looks worn, yet aggressive and violent, true to K&B’s style. It’s a frontier weapon for the exiles of Neterun, built for brutal clashes and ready to tear down as many defenses as possible to support a raider’s main job: eliminate their enemies.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/366bdc153759038ede9194b713a9f3d4219a527d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This concludes our overview of the K&B Beamplier. Stay tuned for the next dev diary.[/p][p]
Farewell, raiders![/p]

notes.title: July Dev Diary #1
notes.notes:
[p]Hello raiders!
[/p][p]After last week's announcement about the early access release, we're really excited. As promised, we're also back with our weekly dev diaries.
[/p][p]In the June entry, we mentioned that we’re working on new modules for raiders to customize their bodies. Today, we want to show you the creation process behind one of those modules: a gatling gun, to be exact.
[/p][p]Meet the [b]Raidgun 230A[/b], born from a concept sketch. As you can see in the image below, we already had a pretty clear vision for this weapon. We wanted something aggressive, worn, and rusty, typical traits of anything that comes from the Imperials. Imagine trying to hold a piece of old scrap metal together. What would you use? We thought of straps, and that detail alone made us instantly love the design.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/37359f18cc521101d2dbebc0865f4314a1731297.jpg"][/img]
When we moved to 3D, we focused on capturing all the small features from the concept: the straps, the spikes to give it a violent feel, the exposed cables, and the barrels ready to fire. The first iterations of the 3D model stayed quite faithful to the concept, though we simplified some parts to improve clarity and in-game readability.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/3f18814b31708ed95da0d8151b8cb59d11b5c094.jpg"][/img]
In the final revision, we pushed the details even further. Now it looks almost lava-powered, like the metal is barely containing the weapon’s energy. The whole piece feels more like a hacked-together module, reinforcing the post-apocalyptic vibe. Here's how it turned out.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/825fe2620ea4bbd15d4b51f95afce779361f3cde.jpg"][/img]
That’s all for now! We'll be back with more in the next dev diary.[/p][p]
Farewell, raiders![/p]

[p]Hello raiders!
[/p][p]The time has come for an important announcement from the depths of the Galaxy of Neterun. [/p][p]We’re thrilled to announce that [i][b]Hell Galaxy[/b][/i] will launch in [b]Early Access on July 31, 2025[/b], where it will remain for about a year.
[/p][p][b]Why this choice?[/b][/p][p]During development, we’ve added a lot of new content to the game. But more importantly, we want [i]Hell Galaxy[/i] to be truly enjoyable for you, our fellow raiders. That’s why we believe it’s essential to build the Galaxy of Neterun together, with your feedback, suggestions, and ideas, shaping a harsh and unforgiving world that you’ll nonetheless come to call home.
[/p][p]We want to connect with our community and refine the experience based on your input. In the Early Access version, you’ll get to try out multiple ship loadouts, explore haunted zones, and dive into main and side quests that reveal the world of [i]Hell Galaxy[/i] through its first two areas: [b]Limbo[/b] and [b]The Core[/b].
[/p][p]With this new phase, our goal is to make [i]Hell Galaxy[/i] a community-driven project. We want to hear your thoughts on balance, pacing, and every other aspect of the game, so we can polish the experience ahead of the full release. That version will include all planned quests, new modules, terrifying creatures, and even more dangerous enemy raiders.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/5254879c2dc2d086f30b150f8360b3214e74e2fe.png"][/img][/p][p]We’re excited to hear what you think and to venture together into the perilous reaches of Neterun, where no raider stands a chance.
[/p][p][b]Join our community on Discord to share your feedback and meet other exiles of Neterun.
[/b][/p][p]Until then...
[/p][p]Farewell, raiders!
[/p][p]The Italian Games Factory Team[/p]

notes.title: June Dev Diary
notes.notes:
[p]Hello raiders!
[/p][p]We're very glad to reconnect with you after all this time. It’s been a while since our last update, but don’t worry. We haven’t been lost in the infernal depths of the Galaxy of Neterun. 

We've just been working behind the scenes on some exciting new things for the project. We’re not quite ready to share them with you just yet, but stay tuned. Over the next few weeks, we’ll start revealing what we’ve been up to.
[/p][p]Now that we’ve resurfaced from the choking grip of our beloved galaxy, we can tell you that weekly dev diary updates are back, starting with this one.
[/p][p]Of course, while we’ve been quiet, work on our harsh universe has continued. We’ll go into more detail in the upcoming diaries, but here’s a quick preview: we’ve been focusing on lighting in some of the more infested areas of Neterun, aiming to strike a balance between creating visually striking environments and ensuring the best possible gameplay experience.

We’ve also been adjusting the aggression levels of alien creatures across the galaxy to make combat feel smoother, and we’ve added a few new modules to expand the ways you can customize your raider’s body. On top of that, we’re adding new quests. There’s a lot about our universe we want you to discover, and we can’t wait for you to dive into it.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/813c3ddf0fb30972b34a787077c68f3ce3e641c4.jpg"][/img][/p][p]That’s it for this dev diary. Stay tuned as we continue building this dangerous, hellish galaxy, until we meet again in the next update.
[/p][p]Farewell, raiders![/p]

notes.title: February Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to our regular dev diary session, our third one this month. Instead of diving into the production details of a specific aspect of the game, we’d like to give you a general update on what we’re currently working on and highlight some key areas of focus.

In the last entry, we talked broadly about lighting in Hell Galaxy. We’ll revisit this topic in the future, but for now, we want to take this opportunity to share some of the changes we’ve been working on to rethink the lighting in certain parts of our beloved Galaxy of Neterun. 
Specifically, we’ve been rebalancing the lighting in a particularly mysterious region of the galaxy, an area where we want to enhance the sense of mystery and make you feel truly lost in a completely hostile environment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/ff0f2b336d368cae0e874b208667e20f0cd9d499.png[/img]
Our goal with this lighting rework is to reinforce the feeling of emptiness that raiders experience when exiled to Neterun. We wanted the raiders to be fierce but also disoriented. Their journey through the Neterun colonies is a metaphorical descent into an increasingly uncertain, perilous, and alien abyss, where dangers lurk around every corner and familiar landmarks grow fewer and farther between. We’re using lighting to emphasize that sense of emptiness, a raider lost in the vacuum of space.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/4cce41d5b7217c3a94d22b6f237718a09b64a939.png[/img]
At the same time, we’re experimenting with a system that provides small clues in the most inaccessible areas, just enough so that you’re not completely alone. 
On the topic of level navigation, in addition to these reference points, we’re also working on ways to make the ship’s radar more useful for navigation. There will be a tutorial on how to use it effectively, along with some small adjustments to ensure it helps you locate key points within each level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/2758e0289aa61f9a520344ef8054a9de181b0481.png[/img]
Lastly, we’re fine-tuning the balance of enemy encounters, adjusting the type, difficulty, and number of enemies in certain areas to keep fights challenging without becoming frustrating.

That’s all for now. As always, we appreciate your support and hope you’ll stay with us for future updates. See you in the next dev diary.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: February Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

We’re back with another dev diary. Today, we want to talk about one of the most important aspects of our worldbuilding: lighting, a key element we’re still refining in search of the perfect balance.

As you can imagine, lighting is one of the most fundamental tools in game design. It adds depth and meaning to the world, shapes the atmosphere, and guides players through both open and confined spaces. Lighting can tell a story on its own, set the tone for different environments, and completely transform the look and feel of a level. 
During the concept phase, we experimented extensively to define the color palettes and explore how lighting could enhance the identity of the various environments you’ll be exploring.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/1bfa63ba702a18fd20366d1abe9f677b82bf8816.png[/img]
In Neterun, we’ve crafted many mysterious locations, places that invite the player to venture further, to uncover what’s lurking behind an asteroid or hidden within a dense nebula. Lighting plays a crucial role in sparking that curiosity, and it must be carefully balanced with other game elements.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/1f89d2b2371bcfb30be08ad6b526dcd9e1c70f29.png[/img]
Some areas of the galaxy felt too dark compared to what we had envisioned, so we’re making adjustments to ensure the lighting enhances the sense of mystery without making navigation too difficult. Our goal is to encourage exploration, whether it’s a distant, eerie glow or the silhouette of a massive, foreboding alien structure shrouded in mist. Lighting allows us to reveal just enough while keeping certain details obscured, and we’re focused on striking the right balance between clarity and intrigue.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/6c30287a8fbe5f5e502424bc5d796c0b4d3641bd.png[/img]
The Neterunian structures in the demo are clearly visible, but what happens when you spot a distant, hostile alien formation, something metallic, something organic? What secrets lie hidden within the swirling mists of Neterun? These are the questions we want to spark in your mind, and lighting helps us craft that sense of mystery.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/711b839f526daa07436b03565cb93111d8b13d6b.png[/img]
That’s all for today. We hope we’ve piqued your curiosity, and we’ll see you in the next dev diary.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: February Dev Diary #1
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to the first dev diary of February. We always enjoy stepping out of our hellish galaxy for a moment to share the concepts and creative process behind every little detail of Neterun. Today, we want to dive into one of the most important structures in the Guild Area of the Galaxy of Neterun: the Harvest Pyramids.

When designing the two guilds of Hell Galaxy, the Gold Guild and the Iron Guild, which we talked about in a previous dev diary, we decided to give them an exclusive area of the galaxy. These guilds emerged shortly after the raiders began colonizing the galaxy, playing a key role in its expansion. 
One of the first tasks for raiders is to gather resources to unlock more powerful upgrades. Anticipating this need, the guilds developed the pyramids, a special technology to harvest Neterun’s valuable resources, which you can see here in an early concept.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/2bc17a37f527b332115472ccec89866a07441a3a.png[/img]
We wanted to associate resource gathering with a symbol of power, which is why we chose the pyramid shape. Each pyramid is stabilized by thrusters that keep it in place. Its smooth surface features a series of collection pockets designed to intercept and store resources. The material used to build these pyramids allows them to withstand the extreme conditions of the Guild Area, while the thrusters ensure they remain in optimal positions for resource gathering. The collection pockets have been a core element of the design since the very first concepts, featuring an interlocking structure that creates a striking, faceted surface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/0f257adeff9525b641f26af5a78e8ff3556b319f.png[/img]
We spent a lot of time refining the placement of the pockets, exploring various concepts to find the most efficient and visually compelling arrangement. Initially, we experimented with pyramids that resembled real-world monuments, featuring intricate reliefs and heavy ornamentation. Our original idea was to make these structures feel more like ancient monuments, as you can see from these early concepts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/f13369fb9479a3a6377a9cc5e9c7518ad15b5a45.png[/img]
Later on, we decided to return to our initial vision, opting for a more layered design that gives the pyramids a distinct, uneven surface. Our goal was not to create a traditional monument but rather something that exists in between a space-age landmark and a functional harvesting structure. This led us to strip away excessive ornamentation, striking a balance between the collection pockets and the other design elements that define the pyramid.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/e8d3d26dfd68ebcac33dd55ce26b2566f56f09c5.png[/img]
And with that, we've reached the end of this dev diary. Time to dive back into Neterun, see you next time when we resurface.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: January Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to the third dev diary of the month. In the previous entries, we took you through the development process behind the Imperial structures of the Galaxy of Neterun. Today, we want to share something similar, focusing on one of the game's most important features: modular ships.

As we mentioned a couple of entries ago, crafting has been a core feature we've wanted in the game since day one. Beyond the mechanics, we also wanted to integrate it into the game's lore in a way that felt both immersive and believable. 
To achieve this, we developed a straightforward technology within the lore of Hell Galaxy that would be instantly recognizable. Drawing inspiration from classic space combat games, we created sockets as a visual and functional foundation for modular ship designs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/52116645a6a00c8a111c5587bc1f6d7066c60d5f.jpg[/img]
For in-game implementation, we aimed to keep the shapes of the sockets simple and universal, as each module serves a distinct purpose. Using square shapes as the base ensured they were instantly identifiable while supporting a system that works seamlessly across all modules. This approach allowed us to design compact ships where the hull naturally integrates with the modules, creating a unified yet visually distinct look.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/ef09d270c924e7cbc6f59d90ad992a3ed9a172f2.jpg[/img]
The goal was to maintain a universal attachment system that works seamlessly across all modules, without compromising the uniqueness of their designs. We started by defining each module's function and then focused on achieving a clean, high-tech aesthetic that makes them easy to identify.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/07ea6430fb64a90531be132ee707164e92efc96a.jpg[/img]
To balance gameplay, we decided to eliminate two types of purchasable modules, those for collecting sonic matter and cargo storage, and instead integrated these functionalities directly into the hull, as we realized that players were often forced to sacrifice valuable attachment slots for weapons or engines in order to accommodate these modules. By integrating them into the hull, we freed up slots for more dynamic builds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/70d529afc53371519f130245bee86f0f76ac8ade.png[/img]
For the modules, we aimed to offer a diverse range of shapes and functions. Some were inspired by classic space combat game archetypes, while others were tailored specifically to the unique universe of Hell Galaxy. We took a similar approach with the hulls, creating a variety of designs to support different builds and aesthetics. This diversity reflects the advanced technological level of the human empire in Neterun's lore, a civilization capable of colonizing even the darkest corners of the universe.

That’s all for this dev diary. We hope you’ve enjoyed this peek into our creative process, and stay tuned for the next entry.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: January Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to this new dev diary. In the first entry of the year, we introduced the Transponder, using it as a way to explore the distinct rationalism of Imperial architecture, which sets it apart from the raiders’ approach. Today, we want to share more concepts of Imperial props and dive deeper into the thought process behind designing the raider colonies of Neterun.

As we mentioned in the last dev diary, the lore of the Galaxy of Neterun envisions colonization unfolding in two phases: an initial period when Imperial explorers were actively charting the galaxy, followed by a second phase dominated solely by raiders. To reflect this history, we created two distinct architectural styles, with Imperial structures characterized by pronounced geometry and a stark contrast to the raiders’ more improvised constructions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/43c52ecfc3197f1eac69b28369e5eb317e5f57ae.png[/img]
Looking at these concepts, you’ll notice that Imperial structures embody a geometric, angular regularity. They’re made up of interlocking blocks that fit together seamlessly, like a massive jigsaw puzzle. This modular design allows them to adapt and integrate with any asteroid or planetoid they encounter. Much of the Empire’s constructed spaces are square and modular, paralleling the raiders’ ship designs in their functionality and versatility.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/d0a2671fd77f48c6c67ca39ed08715ad32c23db1.png[/img]
Key features like magnetic hooks, drills, and spikes allow these structures to anchor themselves into rocky surfaces, targeting areas rich in minerals to extract Neterun’s valuable resources. In our lore, the Human Empire’s dominance stems not only from its capacity for expansion but also from its superior mining capabilities. This is why mining facilities received special attention during the concept phase. We wanted to evoke an environment deeply intertwined with the extraction and utilization of resources.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/d44d97e93fb6af9aff83ccb93a895f5fa016ee1d.png[/img]
In resource-abundant areas, the Empire constructed small mining and transport structures designed for efficiency. Through this architectural storytelling, we sought to convey the early stages of galactic colonization. The rationality, geometry, and layered composition of these Imperial designs narrate a history of humanity shaping its surroundings in pursuit of imperial grandeur. These structures seem to cling to Neterun’s environment, drawing lifeblood from the cosmos for the glory of the Empire.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/9b6345667667b438a2508bdb27bd1a280f9ce601.png[/img]
We love sharing the ideas and inspirations behind even the smallest elements of Hell Galaxy, and we hope you’ve enjoyed it. We look forward to seeing you in the next dev diary.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: December Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to this new dev diary, the last one of December before the holiday season. Today the Hell Galaxy production team would like to share a topic with you that hasn’t been covered before: one of the scariest creatures in Neterun, the Colossi. Please keep in mind that the material we’re sharing is WIP, including concepts and other unfinished elements.

Okay, we admit it, we want to avoid spoilers, so let’s just say that we won’t be going into too much detail. Instead, we’ll show you the development stages of the Colossus featured in the game demo and share some of their lore, as well as our thoughts on them.
The idea of including giant creatures in our IP was one of the first concepts we explored during pre-production. We wanted to create a dangerous galaxy with an aura of mystery, inspired by one of our core design pillars, the cosmic horror. It was natural for us to introduce creatures larger than the players.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/8123b974221a8afae096475d320c8552bb31bd96.jpg[/img]
With the Colossi, we wanted to respect the design principle established for all the creatures in Neterun, the mix of biological and mechanical elements. The Colossi are no exception. They contain sonic matter (and more, but we’re avoiding spoilers!) and are made up of alien mechanical parts that are common throughout the Galaxy of Neterun, along with strange biological manifestations that generate enormous amounts of energy. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/b0f994c1b201da864ecdd9a6f3c9c3c6e9b35eee.png[/img]
Alongside the Alters, the ectoplasmic beings that threaten the mental stability of the raiders, the Colossi are one of the main reasons the Imperial explorers soon realized that Neterun was far more dangerous than they thought. We wanted to convey a sense of fascination, combined with the danger these creatures pose.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/5dd93b4eda3ea3a369d65af4441fd4b8919ba5e7.png[/img]
But we also wanted them shrouded in mystery, distinct from the smaller creatures of Hell Galaxy. Among the colonies of Neterun, no one knows the true nature of the Colossi, how long they’ve existed, or what instincts drive them to roam the galaxy’s darkness. Raiders try to stay away from them, though some are drawn to the mystery they embody. We wanted the Colossi to convey the immense energy that animates them, which is why we equipped the final in-game models with parts that hint at constant energy flows.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/6d32ccc9f7404d2b9231e82b0f23c870c94368cf.png[/img]
And that brings us to the end of this entry. We hope you enjoyed reading it, and we’ll see you next year with another dev diary. Until then, and as always,

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: December Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

This is the Hell Galaxy production team, and we’re pleased to welcome you to the December edition of our dev diary. In recent entries, we’ve focused on worldbuilding and storytelling, showcasing some of the perilous and sinister locations in our galaxy. Today, we’d like to continue that theme by diving into one of the core concepts behind Neterun's worldbuilding: space corruption. Please keep in mind that the material we’re sharing is still a work in progress.

One of the central pillars of our aesthetic, and of our IP as a whole, is the post-apocalyptic theme. We’ve chosen to depict this through the corruption of the environment surrounding the raiders. This environmental corruption parallels the raiders’ own fate: former prisoners condemned to transformation and perpetual exile, stripped of everything they once were or possessed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/d8b4cf3eea4703c6e4f0411e1dad46dcdcbd7807.png[/img]
Many environments in the Galaxy of Neterun reflect this theme. Alien parasites infest mysterious structures, spreading in clusters that invade the landscape and corrupt the minds of those who traverse them. Yet, in some cases, raiders construct places of worship to resist the creeping corruption, even as the boundaries of their own sanity fray. These sanctuaries are mental abysses, where distorted perceptions obscure the difference between safety and peril.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/c8dca50b12b1f79468f69002435ef4d361117fdf.png[/img]
In the concept phase, we decided to reinforce the raiders' sense of eternal exile not only with the humanoid-shaped structures showcased in previous dev diaries, but also with pervasive organic elements. Bulbous growths infect walls and altars, as alien substances crawl and take root. This design choice enhances the eerie atmosphere of Neterun while serving as a visual metaphor for the raiders’ own transformation into biomechanical hybrids. The environments mirror their internal corruption, becoming progressively darker, more hostile, and more hazardous as players advance through the galaxy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/34eb07df10faa165c81536ee22a61d68423a8217.png[/img]
This approach also ties into the player’s sense of progression. As you venture further into the Galaxy of Neterun, corrupted environments become more prevalent. Raider outposts, once safe havens, diminish into isolated refuges within the interstellar void, surrounded by ghosts and predatory creatures. Our aim is to evoke a sense of disorientation, with the transforming landscape reflecting the raiders’ gradual detachment from their humanity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/ab9d0d487bd5543d0114dc4780c0d9541fddc9e8.png[/img]
We hope you found this dev diary insightful and look forward to sharing more in the next one.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: December Dev Diary #1
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to the first Dev Diary of December. While your production team is hard at work making the exile of raiders in Neterun as dreadful as possible, we like to check in with you now and then to share what we’ve been working on. For today's entry, we want to delve deeper into the mysterious race that once inhabited Galaxy of Neterun: the Neterunians.

During the design phase, imagining what the Neterunians might have left behind was an inspiring process. In the first dev diary of November, we showcased some of their ancient structures, and today, we’re continuing down that path. 
One of our primary goals is to ensure that you feel a true sense of discovery when navigating the treacherous spirals of Neterun. This mirrors the experience of the first Imperial explorers who ventured into Neterun, before the raiders arrived.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/4f1e1aa491a91bd769ee94ed8ba72b84dd7268b6.png[/img]
When designing these structures, we aimed to evoke both a sense of wonder and an air of mystery. We also put significant effort into the materials associated with these monuments. Our vision was to create a blend of rocky and organic textures, infused with sonic matter that flows like lifeblood, illuminating the monuments and making them visible from great distances, beacons in the galactic nebula.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/bedd0dfde90b91b23ba4d5dff43e51558d4aa25a.png[/img]
The neterunian structures are designed to tell stories simply through their presence. They invite discovery, leaving players with unanswered questions or intriguing interruptions in an organic narrative where the environment itself is a storyteller. 
This storytelling extends to the raider colonies as well. What are the organic structures that now infect them? Or, from another perspective, what lies beneath the impure metal structures, such as the stations, mines, excavators, and wreckage? What secrets are buried below? As we’ve shown in previous diaries, we paid attention to the violent integration between metal and rock in these environments.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/7fb1770d4cb270d231c7e21b54ebb94182cab62c.png[/img]
The Human Empire, ever opportunistic, repurposed the ancient neterunian structures to build their colonies, sonic matter extraction sites, and other facilities. In doing so, they transformed Neterun into what it is today: a massive prison, haunted by ghosts and riddled with dangers. It's a cannibalization of something ancient and unknowable, something dead for who knows how long, save for the vivid green sonic matter that still pulses through these structures…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/084dc651092df536580edd93a7bce88580f039d1.png[/img]
And that brings us to the end of this dev diary. We look forward to sharing more about our perilous galaxy in the next entry.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: November Dev Diary #5
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

We’ve reached the final dev diary for November. One of the key areas we’ve been focusing on lately is the overhaul of mining in the game. Since this is also an important aspect of the lore, we wanted to share how mining is being implemented in Hell Galaxy.

Every colony established by the Human Empire across the universe has, as one of its core missions, the search and extraction of valuable resources for the Imperials. The dangerous Galaxy of Neterun serves as a prime example: a small galaxy that contains one of the most coveted resources, the so-called sonic matter, whose collection has led to the rise of raiders. But Neterun is also home to other minerals of varying value, which raiders gather and trade with space stations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/78fcf50d33e9d39f7250c675380eb69c18b85e8c.png[/img]
As you progress through the game, you’ll have better chances of finding rare and valuable resources, aligning with the only rule that applies to raiders, the law of the fittest. We’ve tied mining to the core principle of raider survival: the deeper you venture into the dangers of Neterun, the rarer and more valuable the resources you’ll find. The Imperials themselves enforce this mantra of colonization. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/fc6b61caeb5a94f10784cc3477ca3d52b6e9ce7b.png[/img]
Raiders are born to claim the most valuable resources. If you’re strong and ruthless enough to defeat your enemies and survive among the colonies of Neterun, you’ll eventually reach the ultimate prize. That’s why in Limbo, the first area raiders explore after their birth, you won’t find resources of significant value. As you progress as a raider, you’ll unlock access to more lucrative mining opportunities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/c9986c65f5fb2aa76e3fec734e6f25e048d6d49d.png[/img]
In terms of resource distribution, you’ll find both individual mineable resources that you can search for and collect, as well as more valuable and rare resource deposits, which offer raiders an easy way to earn credits. We’re also refining the markers for these deposits to ensure they provide accurate directions without being too intrusive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/dcd2114c85ee474dddbbeec245e4b8e89f4f041d.png[/img]
We can say that resource gathering has never been easy for the Human Empire, which often sacrificed everything to obtain the resources it needed, resources upon which colony space stations were built, creating a vicious cycle of destruction and rebirth in the form of raiders…

But that’s a story for another time. The team behind Hell Galaxy thanks you for your continued support and looks forward to sharing more in the next dev diary.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: November Dev Diary #4
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

The Hell Galaxy development team is pleased to welcome you to another dev diary. 
In the last two entries, we explored the creation of the Extractor and the process of bringing a raider to life. When successful, this process results in a new bio-machine hybrid, ready to endure its exile in Neterun. But what happens when the process fails?

This question guided us as we explored the more fragmented corners of our universe. The result was the creation of the E-Was, failed raiders whose installation process went awry, which we discussed in a previous article. Alongside the E-Was, we envisioned the places where they are abandoned: the Dumps. These eerie graveyards, which we’ll delve into today, have already made an appearance in the game demo.
A Dump represents everything lost when you’re cast into the Galaxy of Neterun. Picture this: you’ve just been extracted, stripped of your past life because the Imperials demand resources. You’ve already lost everything you once were. Your consciousness is sent to another galaxy, but something malfunctions, and you’re left stranded in these raider graveyards, the Dumps.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/86c8bf5a66e2763d39c40326cfdd0f8a4b2a3bc7.png[/img]
The Dumps are fragmented realms of decay. Space debris drifts among crumbling structures that dissolve into the void. While this desolate environment might yield some valuable loot, it more often reveals the remnants of unborn raiders, decomposed hybrids, relics of a vanished humanity. Massive wrecks of capital ships lie dormant. The victorious salvage what they can to rebuild, while the defeated leave behind only faint echoes of lost brainwaves, scattered among the stars.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/767b6ba4eb80fc234953409b8b0f81c0bb7f9336.png[/img]
Visually, the Dumps evoke a sense of desolation. Totem-like antennas, bristling with sharp needles and constructed from cables twisted into rib cage-like shapes, echo the Extractor’s eerie form. Everything here is torn apart, left to decay, a perpetual monument to a failed exile. The Dumps underscore the Imperials’ callous view of raiders as disposable tools. Raiders, eternal prisoners of this galaxy, are left to survive however they can: by forging their own rules and serving their penance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/f7af7bb2f633f0e4d420adf57c4faf58eb68c356.png[/img]
Much like the space stations we built from distorted raider memories post-Extraction, the Dumps were designed to feel even more fragmented. They’re graveyards for the unborn, filled with skeletal remains of failed warriors and heaps of scrap metal scattered on the outskirts of Neterun’s raider colonies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/55de764bbaf60a32d5f5d117cf7a61fc0c3e3bda.png[/img]
That concludes this dev diary, and we look forward to sharing more with you in the next one.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: November Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to the new dev diary for November. In the previous entry, we shared sketches of the work leading to the creation of the Extractor, the entity responsible for bringing a new Raider into existence. Since this moment is so pivotal to our lore, we’d like to dive deeper into this topic today, exploring what happens immediately after the Extraction: the birth, which marks the very first sequence in our story.

Who remembers the moment of their own birth? Likely no one, yet it must be a deeply traumatic process, a moment when something entirely new is brought into existence. Translating this trauma into the experience of a mind trapped in cold, unfeeling metal was our primary goal when conceptualizing the birth of a raider. We wanted the first impression to evoke that sense of shock, isolation and loneliness.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/f072b1116ce2bac263cebe5bf3fda34fbe5c840a.png[/img]
You awaken in the dark and realize you are no longer you. You are a machine. Your first movements are a test to see if you can adapt to this body or if you’re destined to be discarded, a failed experiment sent to a distant galaxy.
This is the first moment. But it doesn’t end there. We wanted the initial sense of isolation to give way to a growing unease about your circumstances. So we envisioned a transition from a solitary room to a larger chamber filled with stations where the process of birthing other Raiders is repeated over and over, endlessly replicated for others who, like you, have been plucked from unknown corners of the universe and reshaped into biological machines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/62e7405a7feb05a08961091f3a57bfa663ad066a.png[/img]
A hive of suffering stands before you. Around you are others like yourself, cast into a cruel and unforgiving galaxy where they must endure the rest of their days. To capture this atmosphere, we also placed emphasis on sound: the distant echoes of screams, reverberating through hollow vessels animated by minds severed from their original bodies. This is what we call the Traverse, the starting point of your journey through Hell Galaxy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/90080db86601db8d2c2c63b936b309f794ed2cbb.png[/img]
Thus, a raider is born: into pain, loneliness, and a brutal existence. In this new reality, only those who seize power can hope to dominate, knowing there is no way back. A raider’s first instinct is to leave the Traverse, because it is the only light at the end of the tunnel. But the Traverse is a tainted womb, beyond which lies no salvation, only the dangers of the Galaxy of Neterun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/d87130f966709e204b0ab1d65a8132e639f35362.png[/img]
And so we conclude this dev diary. We hope you’ve found this glimpse into our creative process intriguing and look forward to sharing more with you in the next entry.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: November Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to another episode of our dev diaries. Today, we’re inviting you into the creative process behind one of the most important pieces of Hell Galaxy lore: the moment a raider is born. Specifically, we’re going to share the creation of the character responsible for this entire process, the Extractor, who appears in the game’s opening cutscene in the demo.

When we began conceptualizing the Extractor, we wanted a character shrouded in mystery, one who would reveal very little. The Extractor is the one who extracts the mind and installs it into a ship; he is the force that brings raiders to life, and we wanted him to embody a sense of both solemnity and royalty.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/dc718ea7e72f9c53b700c250585e797b05dffeba.png[/img]
But that wasn’t all. When we envisioned the extraction scene, we wanted it to be not only solemn but eerie, a “ritual” carried out with makeshift tools in a dimly lit room. To capture this, we gave the Extractor moving limbs that convey the impression of a being that drags itself with stiff, robotic motions through the Hall of Passage, a dark room filled with unsettling instruments. The Hall of Passage is the Extractor’s domain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/899a0d6a6eb2ef45bef46e14738803ee442a3579.png[/img]
Through the Extractor’s deliberate movements, we aimed to convey a sense of inevitability. Those who find themselves under his knife know they won’t return in the flesh. They understand they’re about to be transformed into strange hybrids of gray matter, brain waves, and ship hulls. 
From this concept, it was only natural to give him hands with long, pointed fingers hiding needles. The Extractor’s lethal arm is shrouded in bundles of cables, inspired by the dense, flowing circulatory system depicted in Di Sangro’s eighteenth-century anatomical machines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/fed045707a533b84bc5ea3af9f0c4fd5172996cb.png[/img]
Sound design was also key to portraying the Extractor’s constant, ominous pace as he approaches his chair. By blending these elements, the sounds, the reaching limbs, the regal yet sinister face devoid of eyes or any comforting markers, we brought the Extractor to life as you see him in the demo.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/c449adffc0cce8cd5554876b4065a3b66fe74caf.png[/img]
When you stand before the Extractor, remember: you can scream, or try to calm your breathing, but there’s no escape. Your transformation into an eternal bio-machine hybrid has already begun, and there is no turning back.

With that, we’ve come to the end of this new entry. And since we’ve been talking about the Extractor, today you can say it out loud:

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: November Dev Diary #1
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

We welcome you to a new dev diary. Before we start, we want to thank you for your support and hope you'll find today's entry intriguing. With this late October/early November release, it feels fitting to revisit a topic we introduced in one of our first dev diaries, expanding on it now with more images to share: the most mysterious and alien structures in the Galaxy of Neterun. Keep in mind that everything we show is a work in progress, so some things may change in the final product.

So, let's talk about alien spaces. As introduced in the demo, the galaxy in which Hell Galaxy unfolds is named after an extinct race. When we began developing the environments they left behind, we wanted to combine natural elements with more horrific features, like pierced nests and infected clusters.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/93928e9a0429bcf921a52eb1a8e3a7df109ce4d4.png[/img]
We wanted shapes that would make our raiders feel truly lost in a harsh, inhospitable environment, where landmarks are scarce and structures emerging from the sonic matter clouds unsettle rather than comfort. We contrasted these twisted, surreal geometries with natural landmarks to reflect the raiders' own, more familiar structures. Our aim is to convey a remote, hostile space, where life barely survives in bizarre structures, where dangerous galactic creatures nest in the shadows.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/2ab755af8eba2e7bdc9956021eca1075696777d1.png[/img]
Our concepts include wrinkled, layered structures that seem to have formed over time, and columns lost in the mists of an inhospitable world. We crafted spaces that make it hard to gauge scale at a glance, where the distant light of stars, a glimmer of hope, is obscured by looming, menacing structures. Here, clusters of creatures lie in wait, showing no mercy to the unfortunate invaders who dare to enter. These are the structures we use to convey the idea of Neterun as a giant prison, where exile condemns you to a place where hope does not exist and landmarks are lost.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/c553f4a190579935c4b513ca8a699193e6294614.png[/img]
Sonic matter is what keeps these structures and the creatures within them alive, an enigmatic mass made of the forgotten forms of an extinct race and the new infections taking hold of these abandoned remnants. We may be tough on our raiders, but rest assured, there are things in Neterun even crueler than us…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/30de9b5dc388890eb6c70e136f981ea4c7072deb.png[/img]
With this spectral goodbye, we close the first November Diary and look forward to sharing more in the next entry.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: October Dev Diary #4
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to another dev diary. In the last entry, we shared a general (and yes, still partial...) update on our recent production efforts. Today, the team wants to introduce you to another creature from the strange ecosystem of Neterun: the Lepisma. Please keep in mind that everything we show you is a work in progress and may change in the final product.

The Lepisma got its name from the raiders of the Malaxdon cult, who were the first to detect the presence of these elusive creatures. When conceptualizing the Lepisma, we wanted to design an exception to Neterun's usual dangers, a creature that, unlike others we've showcased in previous diaries, is non-aggressive. Similar to the Morays, another Neterunian species we discussed a couple of diaries ago, the Lepisma’s name reflects its distinctive shape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/cb17c992e7f032246b8d0c799924c8f5c43431d3.jpg[/img]
Since then, the Lepisma’s design has changed only slightly, as our initial concept allowed us to capture its form with little need for additional iterations. Like other creatures of Neterun, the Lepisma features a mechanical component that is closely tied to sonic matter, though it stands out for its gentler nature in comparison to the more aggressive Morays and Zanions. These creatures inhabit one of the galaxy's most mysterious areas and prefer to avoid raiders rather than engage them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/30250c8f00a8a723daf07232eff6f2c203008b07.jpg[/img]
With this in mind, we’ve crafted the Lepisma with a much more cautious behavior, adding an element of calm to our hostile galactic prison. Drawn to the massive structures left behind by the ancient Neterunians, the Lepisma uses them not as hunting grounds but as shelter, slipping into the shadows to evade raiders. Thanks to its connection to sonic matter, it moves swiftly and elusively, using these structures both for navigation and defense.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/b387464e5af719ea5db59435d0cecb2a4b6ac5d3.png[/img]
Lepisma live in packs that migrate from zone to zone, moving in unison along the energy fields generated by Neterunian monuments. These fields help them stay in sync and remain shielded from raiders and other threats. As a result, the Lepisma represents an anomaly within Neterun’s typically aggressive wildlife. It’s a creature only partly influenced by the violence of sonic-matter life forms.

That’s all for today. We’ve reached the end of this October dev diary, but we hope to be back soon with another entry. Until next time,

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: October Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

It's great to meet again in this new dev diary. Work on our beloved galaxy is progressing with great enthusiasm, and we're excited to share that energy with you as we continue developing this project. Please keep in mind that the images we show you are works-in-progress, so some elements may change in the final product.

Today's diary doesn't focus on a specific topic, but rather provides an update on various areas of development we're currently working on. From time to time, we like to give you these broader updates to take a step back from the many dangers lurking in Neterun.
One of the tasks we're focusing on is making minor adjustments to the environments you'll be exploring in the final game. We're not making any major changes (we love the spaces we're building), but we do want to introduce some small dynamic elements into the world. In certain areas of the game, we're adding subtle details that will only become visible after you complete specific missions. The raider colonies scattered across the Galaxy of Neterun are always in a state of unrest, and it's easy to come across skirmishes over a supply station blockade or the spread of strange biological growths.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/44761771/e91f3a5032dd7f57e1dab1c05ae2ffbd4e2e0326.jpg[/img]
These additions also give us a chance to refine the navigability of the levels and perhaps introduce some new enemy groups that weren’t there before. Recently, we've populated one of Neterun's most mysterious regions, where interstellar clouds conceal forgotten structures and haunted ruins, with new groups of creatures.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/44761771/b462db5d4c79208894be138d72dd7d277eb8a34e.png[/img]
Speaking of creatures, we’re also tweaking some of their attacks, such as the sonic matter ray of the gunlaxies, which we introduced in a previous dev diary. Our goal is to make combat fun, not frustrating, but sometimes we get a little carried away and end up tormenting our raiders more than we intended, creating battles that are… well, brutal. However, we don’t want to be too mean, so we’re working hard to ensure that the creatures you encounter strike a balance between fun and challenge. Fun, but also a little dangerous, of course.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/44761771/895081c82a6ac9edb823e2ebada53c1f7a87c6fc.png[/img]

And with that ongoing battle against the gunlaxies’ relentless rays, we’ve reached the end of this dev diary. We’ll be back soon with more updates, but until then, you’ll find us lurking in the perilous neterunian ruins.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: October Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to the new October Dev Diary. In the last two entries, we introduced you to the creation process of two creatures that inhabit the Galaxy of Neterun. Today, we’re continuing that series by discussing an enemy many of you who played the demo are already familiar with: the Zanion. As always, please remember that the material we’re about to show you is still in development.

Let’s dive into the creation of the Zanion. This is the very first creature that new raiders will encounter in their journey through the Galaxy of Neterun, so we wanted to design something powerful, but not overwhelmingly so. The Zanion’s aggressiveness has increased since earlier versions, and its appearance has evolved, as you can see from one of the initial models we created, somewhat different from the current version.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/eee3800d44ea7372b45875d128144793d46b98d7.jpg[/img]
As you’ll notice in the picture, the inspirations for the Zanion came from nature, particularly the world of spores and fungi. We envisioned a creature that uses sonic matter to produce large spores, which explode on contact with the raider's body. These spores are created in the central part of the creature, in a kind of pouch on its back, reminiscent of earthball mushrooms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/423c2e862a6928930558b2dd6cdd6588e46ddbab.jpg[/img]
The structure on its head, on the other hand, serves to absorb tiny particles of sonic matter, which the Zanion then processes to both form and launch the spores.
Originally, the Zanion was designed to be a fairly passive creature, easily hunted by raiders seeking to collect sonic matter. Over time, however, we transformed them into much more aggressive beings, though they remain less hostile than the Gunlaxy, which we discussed in the last dev diary. Being surrounded by a group of Zanion is never ideal for a raider. In combat, you’ll have to contend with their explosive spores.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/40df65fad0085b386b04e1daa9a83962e588ee82.png[/img]
One of the Zanion’s defining traits is its defensive behavior. However, if you persist in chasing and shooting at them, no Zanion will show you mercy, and you’ll soon find yourself dodging an overwhelming barrage of dangerous spores. But hey, you brought it upon yourself.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/3e9cb0124381d10d0827618290125cdf330db0ab.png[/img]
That brings us to the end of this dev diary. We hope you enjoyed it and look forward to sharing more in the next diary.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: October Dev Diary #1
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

This is your dedicated team reaching out from the depths of our dangerous galaxy to connect with all of you who follow us so passionately.
In this new dev diary, we’re going to share the process behind creating another creature you’ll encounter in the game, known to the raider colonists as the gunlaxy. Some of you might remember seeing a glimpse of it a few diaries ago. Please keep in mind that what we’re showing you is still a work in progress, and things may change in the final product.

As you know from previous dev diaries, we’ve based our creature designs on a fusion of biology and mechanics. However, we wanted to explore something entirely biological this time, leading us to experiment with a creature that doesn’t have any obvious mechanical components, and thus, the gunlaxy was born.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/6ac613130340a258da47fede656d8646cd361a81.png[/img]
The Imperial explorers who first encountered a gunlaxy during the early colonization of Neterun gave it its name because of its unique attack style. We designed the creature with an internal organ that concentrates sonic energy into a beam, alongside small vents that can fire sonic matter projectiles, hence the name it’s now known by among raiders.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/438ea5b6258159c8963584a8b351b22caa8b1a6a.png[/img]
Though the gunlaxy doesn’t have highly developed vision, it compensates with incredibly sensitive antennae covering its body. These antennae can detect not only biological creatures but also many of the machines that roam the Galaxy of Neterun. This means that raiders, with all their metal enhancements, are far from safe when faced with this creature.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/0918a571dc1c3f8590fbb957577738c455a3dc8d.png[/img]
Gunlaxies are much more protective of their nests compared to the morays we discussed in the last dev diary. The moment their antennae pick up on potential danger near their nest, they’ll attack anyone they perceive as a threat. In short, if a raider stumbles into a cluster of gunlaxy nests, they’ll need every bit of their survival skills to get out with their metal bodies intact.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/67850e091fbf384cdd6bfc9114442aeca48ecfae.png[/img]
With this exploration into the world of Neterunian biology, we’ve reached the end of this dev diary. We hope you enjoyed it and look forward to sharing more in the next entry.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: September Dev Diary #4
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

Welcome to the final diary in our September series. Over the past few weeks, we’ve shared details about some of the raid types you’ll encounter in the game and the creative process behind their design. Today, we’ll talk about creation again, but this time we’re focusing on creatures, specifically, one type you'll come across in the Galaxy of Neterun: the Morays.
As always, we want to remind you that the material we share is a work in progress, and some aspects may change as development continues.

Let’s dive into the creatures of Neterun. In one of the earlier dev diaries, we introduced the core concept behind the planet’s biology, a fusion of organic and metallic elements, powered by sonic matter. The moray creatures fit perfectly within this framework, as you can see in one of the first iterations we designed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/809aff6d7b7e3b444d3669e2e07668369bab5d30.jpg[/img]
In this version, you can clearly observe the blend of biology and mechanics. Raiders named them "Morays" because of their shape, after early Imperial explorers first encountered these hostile beings while venturing into Neterun, quickly realizing they were unwelcome intruders in the creatures' territory. Morays are fiercely protective of their habitat, and you’ll find them both in groups and on their own as they patrol the more remote regions of Neterun. We wanted them to evoke a sense of looming danger, with their glowing eyes biding their time until they strike.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/bfec3e1173d73cae8323bce53cf0b5b589b96651.png[/img]
As you can imagine, coexisting with these creatures isn't easy for the raiders. Morays are highly aggressive and use sonic matter to fuel a wide array of attacks against any raiders unfortunate enough to cross their path. Our goal was to create a creature that is constantly charged with energy, with luminous patterns running across its leathery body. During combat, the moray channels this energy, through sonic matter, both to shield its vulnerable areas and to amplify its attacks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/1b4ebcb19eba40b1b8f60fa84bf7e1350a38eee5.png[/img]
We designed the morays to feel like predators that circle their prey before moving in for the kill, making them challenging to defeat. Their metallic parts serve as protective armor, guarding their more vulnerable areas while they charge up for an attack. So, raiders, if you ever come across one of these creatures, surviving the encounter might not be so easy…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/e997b0ee3a4a9442e4697f95c14ce08fb5504011.jpg[/img]
And with that, we've come to the end of this dev diary. We hope you enjoyed this glimpse into yet another deadly threat from our hellish galaxy. We’ll see you in the next one!

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: September Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

We're back with more stories from the development of Hell Galaxy. In the last dev diaries, we gave you a peek into the process of designing some of the ships in the game. Today, we’re expanding on that by introducing some hulls we haven't covered yet: capital ships.

Capital ships are typically massive vessels, operated by large crews and heavily armed. But this is the Galaxy of Neterun: no humans here, only raiders.
We started with the story. Since capital ships are considered the most significant and powerful vessels, we figured that only a raider with exceptional concentration could command such a large ship. We wanted these ships to serve as status symbols of power, so naturally, Old Joe, overseer of the imperial colonies in Neterun, commands the largest capital ship fleet.
For those of you who’ve played the demo, you’ve already encountered one of the capital ships from Old Joe’s fleet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/10cb39abd97e812c1707d574e1440364358337c0.png[/img]
We wanted the capital ship to represent not just power, but also the intense focus required to operate it. That’s why each capital ship features multiple control, defense, and attack systems.
The main offensive strength of a capital ship comes from its turrets. Positioned on both sides of the ship, these turrets have a high rate of fire, unleashing a relentless barrage of projectiles on the enemy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/a7802b16ccdd28d2caa5c914b41d31d8a00c786e.png[/img]
The turrets themselves are protected by a dual-shield system, providing solid defense. These shields guard not only the ship's weaponry, but also its core, the very heart of the ship that powers all of its systems.
The core is the ship’s vital nerve center. It drives the internal mechanics and safeguards the part of the ship that houses the consciousness of Old Joe. We designed it this way to reflect the resilience of the ship, mirroring the toughness of the raider who commands it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/242e032765889fdd0634c438cfd261303f2dd18a.png[/img]
Old Joe has managed to create an entire fleet of capital ships, each one controlled by fragments of his own brainwaves. This allows him to operate multiple ships at once. We also wanted to convey the idea of Old Joe as a raider who has fought countless battles across the Neterun colonies, so don’t be surprised if you come across the wreckage of his ships scattered throughout the galaxy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/e8f987e18a756e0a82e7720e684ee0a210b12e63.png[/img]
These wrecks are relics of past battles, tough clashes that Old Joe may have lost, but thanks to his large fleet, he never completely disappeared.

That brings us to the end of this dev diary. We hope you’ll continue to support us and stay tuned for the next one.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: September Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

We’re excited to bring you a new dev diary and to reconnect with you through this latest update. In previous diaries, we discussed the creation of certain types of raiders, how they were shaped by gameplay needs, narrative inspiration, and more. In this entry, we’ll continue exploring the creation of raiders, focusing on those most closely tied to Old Joe, a character you met in the demo, as well as those responsible for transportation and construction within the Imperial colonies of the Galaxy of Neterun.

Old Joe presents himself as the Imperial’s right-hand man in the vast exile colony of Neterun. Under his command are a number of raiders who, shortly after their birth, chose to align with Old Joe for protection, aiding him in his efforts to maintain order, conduct trade with space stations, and more. For this reason, we wanted to design raiders who were recruited almost immediately after their creation. We started with the base body model and enhanced it with various weapon types.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/c82bd7f8112a1b99565b6d3b5ddf566584e08ad7.png[/img]
Through this approach, we aimed to reflect the concept of raiders who never sought their own path in Neterun. Traumatized by the Extraction and its aftermath, they essentially become empty vessels from birth. These raiders assist Old Joe not out of loyalty or ambition but because they feel they have no other purpose in the Galaxy of Neterun beyond serving the strongest. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/b95cca7886eb1f4300dff759201ecb45b514a345.png[/img]
Old Joe has little patience for newborn raiders who fail to find their own way. Many perish on dangerous missions, while a few manage to rise to powerful positions despite their harsh start. Those who succeed evolve, acquiring formidable weaponry, heavily armored bodies, and advanced ships, becoming the Imperial military force within the colonies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/ce9f764bdf44dae6da394efb61b8affd65567f72.png[/img]
And what about transport and construction? Drones are often used, but Old Joe also employs raiders who are unfit for combat or the collection of sonic matter, assigning them to cargo ships. We decided that these ships wouldn’t have traditional raider bodies but would instead be integrated into the infrastructure of Imperial bases and stations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/e90fa530af06786b9bed4685bd83c299b326b67f.png[/img]
After extraction, their brain waves are diminished but not entirely gone. These cargo ships haul materials, perform tasks at space stations, and handle trade operations. They are functional consciences, trapped in metal cages from which they will never escape.

With that, we’ve reached the end of this diary. We hope you found it intriguing and look forward to the next update.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: September Dev Diary #1
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

This is your game production team, back with a new development diary. Today, we want to introduce another raider class you’ll come across: the bounty hunters. The images you are about to see show some work in progress.

As you know, the raider ecosystem (if we can call it that) is self-regulating. Bounty hunters play a crucial role in maintaining this balance. If a raider steps out of line or becomes undesirable, someone will place a bounty on their body, and bounty hunters will ensure that raider is either eliminated... or dies trying.
In a hostile environment like the Galaxy of Neterun, we wanted our bounty hunters to be truly dangerous. That’s why we equipped them with heavily armed ships, built to take down their targets. Take J, for instance, the bounty hunter you encountered in the demo.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/3af9c30afa2de2a533a53a42231bc729d626bfa9.png[/img]
J's body comes equipped with multiple rocket launchers, giving his prey almost no chance of escape. When designing J, we envisioned a bounty hunter with an aggressive edge, so we gave his ship a menacing look, reflecting his dangerous, battle-hardened nature.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/29636bf3be72d146195f1781edf95801d0c30010.png[/img]
We took a similar approach when designing the other bounty hunters you’ll face throughout the game. Their sole mission is to kill their targets because there’s no “capture alive” option on Neterun. Bounty hunters use their earnings to upgrade their gear, and many of them are ex-convicts, guilty of violent crimes.
We wanted their bodies to reflect this ruthless mindset. The bounty hunters roam freely throughout the Imperial colonies of Neterun, hiding in the shadows before attacking their targets as a group. Bounty hunters are still raiders, and they often use these hunting parties to settle personal grudges or simply to prove who’s the strongest.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/693b705c6f84455edbfd1ebfd621fd475b7580f6.png[/img]
While they may not all have J’s rocket launchers or his recovery abilities, they are still a serious threat to any raider. Whether you’re heading into a dark, dangerous corner or trying to assist another raider, you may suddenly find yourself ambushed by a pack of bounty hunters, ready to tear you apart and scatter your brainwaves across the cosmic void. Yours and those of their rivals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/6e7cbce703619958c795fb9144b78288afa5194b.png[/img]
That concludes the first dev diary for September. We can’t wait to share more with you in the next one. Thanks for following along, and we hope you stick with us on this journey.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: August Dev Diary #3
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!

We’re excited to bring you a new dev diary, the last one for August. 
In this entry, we want to take you through the creation process of one of the raider classes you’ll encounter in the full version of Hell Galaxy: the Malaxdon. We don't want to reveal too much of the lore (yes, we’re avoiding spoilers), but we do want to share some of the initial concepts behind their development and show you how we translated these ideas into the game’s aesthetic while staying true to its style and narrative.

During development, we realized that it would be interesting to create a group of raiders that function as a kind of cult. In fact, the Malaxdon are exactly that, a cult. Our first task was to give them an aesthetic that would set them apart from the more imperial, chaotic structures made of piled metal, twisted shapes, and so on. We decided to go in the opposite direction, as you can see in this Malaxdon structure (which you may have noticed in some images from previous dev diaries).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/291d87dfbaabca1f159098870a42e26aa22271ec.png[/img]
At first glance, you'll notice a certain geometric precision compared to the Imperial structures. We use very clean pieces of metal as a base, with recognizable shapes that are repeated to form structures reminiscent of cult buildings. You could think of these structures as temples, clean, decorative, and purposeful. By using perfectly smooth and recognizable shapes, we aim to give players a completely different impression when they see a Malaxdon structure compared to an Imperial one.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/0ad118c8d6085cdfeaf2fc735da7ae0c918d0553.png[/img]
The contrast is immediate: on the one hand, there are the imperial space stations that evoke the worst memories of the Extraction; on the other, the templar structures of a raider group that worships the galaxy. Essentially, the Malaxdon offer a different perspective on exile, with their minds united in pursuit of the same goal, isolating themselves from other raiders and fiercely defending their territory.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/21dcd361ae59f377d6e75107e85ead629ff0c598.png[/img]
With this in mind, once we had established the basic concepts for their structures, we decided that the design of the Malaxdon ships should echo that of their buildings. This idea reinforces the concept of a cult that identifies with its structures. That’s why we designed the Malaxdon base ship with similar geometric shapes, reminiscent of the structures at the heart of a Malaxdon station.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44761771/85ccf487c1406dee0f4176ef6ec8b82af364df1a.png[/img]
And that brings us to the end of today’s entry. Remember, what we’ve shown you are still works in progress. We hope you enjoyed this new dev diary and are excited for what’s to come.

Farewell, raiders!

notes.title: August Dev Diary #2
notes.notes:
Hello raiders!
